After a performed re-establishment by effort (more than return.moderateMaxDays since the last executed exposure), the earlier count, block-boundary set included, comes back at most one set per executed week, never at once, whatever the state mode at the re-establishment (known load, pending establishment log, unlogged or re-established) (D53, resolved).

The regain base is the re-establishment count before its phase reduction: min(goal sets for the role, 2, the count the exercise would otherwise have that day). A re-establishment reduced by its phase is followed by that count itself, as a phase-reduced return step 2 is followed by the step-2 count (Q1, reading A).

The cap rises by one set only after a week whose last executed exposure of the exercise executed its whole count (executed sets equal to its count before the phase reduction, gate ADVANCE or EARNED, a logged set); a week whose executed row was below that count, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, never raises it. A phase week whose reduction did not bring the row below that count counts as a whole executed week.
Every later count stays at or below the cap, with phase reductions on top, and is never more than one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment.
Load: a logged load at or after the re-establishment becomes the reference only by the existing adoption rules, never above the re-establishment ceiling (D44, D45).
To be declared in the next policy revision: setsAfterReestablishment states the base before the phase reduction and the whole-count rule, in the words of strengthReturnSets.

D56 (required before any freeze is accepted; not met at R7A-FREEZE-2): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when an executed exposure of the exercise that week executed the count before its phase reduction after its time fit (sets after the fit equal to that count). A week whose executed exposures were all fitted below that count neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps), so the next count stays at most one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment or the return. The return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is already read this way (R20). Regression tests: my D56 timelines (one strength day of 25 minutes, re-establishment in week 7, budget raised to 75 minutes after week 8) and the S6 fitted-regain grid with a raised budget (16 jumps at R7A-FREEZE-2, 0 at R7A-FREEZE-1).

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

Every strength row, the re-establishment row included, takes its day phase once: sets = min(row cap, phase dose of the count the exercise would otherwise have that day), reps in reserve >= max(row floor, phase minimum); the day phase follows days to the race (proximitySemantics).

Race window and post-event: main lifts only, at most raceWeekStrengthSets / postEventStrengthSets set(s) at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir; one race-window session at most, on the strength day furthest from the race and none in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days. Taper and specific rows keep RIR >= 3 (D54, resolved).

A re-establishment row is never above min(goal sets for its role, 2) and never above the phase dose of the exercise's own count that day; it may be below min(goal sets, 2) when that phase dose or the exercise's own count is lower (consolidation, specific, a known dose of 1 set) (Q2).
At a re-establishment the load stays effort-guided under the earlier ceiling; no load increase, new exercise or rotation in taper or race week.
The final validation rejects any strength row above its day phase dose or below the phase minimum reps in reserve, whatever branch built it.

Item 5: a return-entry week is one in which an exercise in use that week is at the entry step; an exercise not in use (rotated out and still parked at the entry step) has no weight. A never-performed exercise, a substitute included, first prescribed after every exercise in use has passed the entry step is established by effort, at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3, with no load converted, and then progresses as a new exercise (NR-21, SUB-6).

D55 (met at R7A-FREEZE-2): an exercise first set up while the exercises in use are in the return steps of a moderate or long return earns no block-boundary set for the block of the return, as return-entry and return-step exposures do not; after the return steps its count rises at most one set per executed week, up to its normal count (its ceiling under strengthReturnSets), with phase reductions on top. Regression tests: the RS2 scenario (return step 2 in a block-end week, a substitution window) for HYPERTROPHY, STRENGTH and RUNNING_SUPPORT, with EVERY_2_WEEKS (parked exercises) and FIXED rotation.

Item 6: sets logged without repetitions leave the repetition target neither met nor missed; the dose holds without a regression step and repetitions are never adopted from a missing value; a logged reserve below the prescription minus one, or fewer sets than prescribed, remains a missed target.

Item 7: a week whose last executed row of an exercise is below its count before the phase reduction, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, earns no regain, return-cap or return-ceiling set.
Item 8: a missed session moves only to a later chosen day of the same sport whose day phase, by days to the race, equals its own; no move in taper or race week; race touches and shakeouts never move.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 (non-blocking; not met at R7A-FREEZE-2): in a short return (at most return.shortMaxDays days) the first quality slot still ahead of the review, the same day included, runs easy (R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN condition 7); until fixed, the same-day short-return case is outside this approval.

S4: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (required before any freeze is accepted; not met at R7A-FREEZE-2): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when an executed exposure of the exercise that week executed the count before its phase reduction after its time fit (sets after the fit equal to that count). A week whose executed exposures were all fitted below that count neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps), so the next count stays at most one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment or the return. The return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is already read this way (R20). Regression tests: my D56 timelines (one strength day of 25 minutes, re-establishment in week 7, budget raised to 75 minutes after week 8) and the S6 fitted-regain grid with a raised budget (16 jumps at R7A-FREEZE-2, 0 at R7A-FREEZE-1).
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed.
